name: agentdock
readme_excerpt:
# AgentDock

**Local-first orchestration platform for coding agents.** AgentDock is not
another coding agent — it is the control plane and worker runtime that lets you
run, monitor, control, test, review, and expose projects worked on by
OpenCode, Codex, Claude Code, Pi, Copilot CLI, or any generic CLI agent.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CLI[CLI] <--> API[Control plane\nREST + SSE]
    WEB[Dashboard] <--> API
    API <--> RT[JobRuntime]
    RT --> OC[OpenCode] & CX[Codex] & CL[Claude] & PI[Pi] & CP[Copilot] & GEN[Any CLI]
```

Fundamental abstraction: **Agent → Workspace → Job → Artifact → Surface → Device**.

## Quick start (Ubuntu/Linux)

```bash
git clone <repo> && cd agentdock
./scripts/install.sh     # node 22+, deps, build, links `agentdock`
agentdock init
agentdock doctor
agentdock serve &         # control plane + local worker on 127.0.0.1:8787
agentdock project add ~/my-project
agentdock run --agent opencode --project <id> --prompt "Add a health endpoint and tests"
agentdock attach <job>    # live output; type to send follow-ups
```

Dashboard: http://127.0.0.1:8787/ (works over SSH port-forward).

Zero-cost smoke test (no model calls):

```bash
agentdock test-agent run --project <id>
agentdock artifacts <job> && agentdock preview <job>
```

## CLI

```bash
agentdock status | agents | workers | projects | jobs
agentdock run --project P --agent codex --prompt "…" [--model M] [--mode worktree|main|temp]
agentdock logs <job> [--follow] | attach <job> | stop <job>
agentdock artifacts <job> | open <job> | preview <job> | events <job>
agentdock review <job> --kind visual
agentdock devices | device install <serial> <artifact> | device screenshot <serial>
agentdock agent add my-agent --command my-agent   # new agents without core changes
```

Every command supports `--json`.

## Setup per agent

| Agent | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode (reference) | `opencode` on PATH; optional `OPENCODE_SERVER_URL` (+`_USERNAME`/`_PASSWORD`) | Uses `opencode run --format json`; attaches to your server when configured. Never exposed publicly. |
| Codex | `codex` on PATH + your own login | `codex exec --json`; respects your existing auth. |
| Claude | `claude` on PATH + your own login | `claude -p --output-format stream-json`; SDK integration optional later. |

name: blindfold-chess
readme_title: Blindfold Chess — voice-first chess for Android
readme_excerpt:
# Blindfold Chess — voice-first chess for Android

Play complete chess games without looking at the board. You speak moves,
the app validates them against a real rules engine, a local engine replies,
and Android Text-to-Speech speaks the answer.

```
APP:  "Your move."
YOU:  "Knight f3."
APP:  "Knight f3."
APP:  "Knight c6."
YOU:  "Bishop b5."
```

## Features

- Voice-first blindfold play: push-to-talk (default) or continuous mode
- Natural chess phrasing ("e4", "knight to f3", "castle kingside", "O-O")
- Ambiguity handling ("Which knight? Knight from d2 or h2.")
- Full rules via chesslib: castling, en passant, promotion, check/mate,
  stalemate, insufficient material, threefold repetition, fifty-move rule,
  FEN, PGN, move history
- Local Stockfish opponent (UCI) with strength/depth/time settings,
  plus a built-in sparring engine fallback so the game always works
- Board queries: "What is on e4?", "Where is my queen?",
  "What is attacking e5?", "Describe the board.", material, last moves…
- Move confirmation mode, undo/redo, repeat, resign
- Game history with review (board, FEN, PGN, export, play-this-position)
- Dark, screen-reader-friendly UI; board hidden by default
- Offline-first, no accounts, no servers

## Build / install

Requirements: JDK 17, Android SDK (platform 34, build-tools 34), Gradle 8.7.

```bash
export ANDROID_HOME=~/Android/Sdk
export PATH=$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools:$PATH
# uses system gradle; wrapper jar intentionally not vendored
gradle :app:assembleDebug
adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
```

Run unit tests (pure JVM, no device needed):

```bash
gradle :app:testDebugUnitTest
```

## Stockfish setup (optional, recommended)

The app plays out of the box with its built-in sparring engine. For full
Stockfish strength, place device binaries at:

```
app/src/main/assets/stockfish/arm64-v8a/stockfish
app/src/main/assets/stockfish/armeabi-v7a/stockfish
app/src/main/assets/stockfish/x86_64/stockfish
```

name: book-copilot
readme_excerpt:
# Book Copilot — READ · COMPRESS · REMEMBER

Two experiences: **READ** (AI-assisted reading environment) and **COMPRESS**
(local-first nonfiction compression engine).

## Quickstart

```bash
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up --build
# web http://localhost:3000 · api http://localhost:8000
```

Local model (default, zero extra config): install llama.cpp, then run its
**server** (not `llama-cli` — that's the interactive chat tool; `llama-server`
is the HTTP server from the same project and speaks the OpenAI-compatible API):

```bash
llama-server -hf openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B-GGUF -ngl 99 -c 8192
# serves http://localhost:8080/v1 — exactly what AI_BASE_URL points at
```

That's it — upload a book and Compress. `-c 8192` gives the section
compression calls headroom. With a cloud key instead, point `AI_BASE_URL` /
`AI_MODEL` / `AI_API_KEY` at OpenAI, OpenRouter, etc.

PDF reading uses a real PDF engine (PDF.js, same as Firefox): full layout,
thumbnails + outline sidebar, zoom, find-in-page. Selecting text in the PDF
feeds the Copilot toolbar exactly like the text view (toggle PDF/Text at the
top of the reader). Original files are stored on upload and served back via
`GET /books/{id}/file`; uploads now report `"indexed": true/false` instead of
ever 500ing on a good parse.

Without a reachable model the copilot runs in offline Socratic mode and the
compression pipeline uses a deterministic extractive fallback (schema-valid,
so the whole flow stays testable with no GPU).

## How it maps to the brief

- **Books**: PDF + EPUB upload, library, chapters/sections, resume position (`current_chapter/offset` saved on navigation).
- **Reader**: clean serif typography, chapter nav, text selection → floating toolbar, highlights, anchored notes, persistent position.
- **Copilot**: Explain / Challenge / Connect / Apply / Ask. Selection is primary context; backend enriches with surrounding text, pgvector-retrieved related passages, book metadata, notes/highlights/memory, prior interactions.
- **Chapter Review**: key ideas, reader questions, recall check (no answers), misunderstandings, concepts, connections to earlier chapters. **Test Me** generates questions, waits for your answers, then grades — never reveals upfront.
- **Reader Memory**: `memory` table (concept/claim/question/interpretation/uncertainty + confidence) fed by interactions; designed for a future cross-book knowledge graph (add `book_id=NULL` global view + entity edges).

## Architecture

```
apps/web  Next.js 14 + TS + Tailwind + Zustand (selection/copilot state)
apps/api  FastAPI + SQLAlchemy + pgvector (single Postgres, no extra vector DB)
packages/shared  shared TS types
```

AI abstraction: `app/services/ai.py` → `AIProvider` / `OpenAICompatibleProvider` (env: `AI_BASE_URL/MODEL/KEY` — OpenRouter default, OpenAI, Ollama all work).
Embeddings: `app/services/embeddings.py` → `ApiEmbedding` / `HashEmbedding` (`EMBEDDING_MODE=local|api`). Local is a deterministic trigram-hash vector so RAG + docker work with zero keys.

## API sketch

- `POST /books/upload` · `GET /books` · `GET /books/{id}` · `GET /books/{id}/chapters/{i}` · `POST /books/{id}/position`
- highlights / notes CRUD · `POST /copilot` · `POST /books/{id}/chapters/{i}/review` · `POST .../quiz` · `POST .../quiz/grade` · `GET/POST /books/{id}/memory`

name: bullet_engine
readme_title: Bullet Chess Engine — practical winning probability for very fast time controls
readme_excerpt:
# Bullet Chess Engine — practical winning probability for very fast time controls

`Position -> Stockfish candidates/eval -> feature extraction -> Bullet Move Scoring Model -> move selection`

Stockfish remains the source of objective truth. The decision layer asks:
**"Given this position, which move is most likely to win this bullet game against a
time-pressured opponent?"** All "psychology" features are labeled experimental
proxies, not claims about human cognition.

## Quick start

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
# Stockfish: bundled at ./bin/stockfish (or set BULLET_STOCKFISH=/path/to/stockfish)
export BULLET_STOCKFISH=$(pwd)/bin/stockfish

# Web analysis platform (recommended)
python scripts/web.py --port 8000
# → open http://127.0.0.1:8000

# UCI (Cutechess / Arena / lichess-bot style GUIs)
python -m bullet_engine bullet
# or
python scripts/uci_engine.py bullet

# Analyze a position with explanation
python scripts/analyze.py --fen "r1bqk2r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/2b1p3/2B1P3/5N2/PPPP1PPP/RNBQK2R w KQkq - 4 4" --profile bullet

# Benchmark (10 curated positions, prints candidate table)
python scripts/benchmark.py --profile bullet --depth 10

# Self-play: bullet profile vs raw stockfish, 60+1
python scripts/self_play.py --white bullet:bullet --black stockfish --rounds 2 --base 60 --inc 1

# Tests
python -m pytest tests/ -x -q
```

## UCI options

| Option | Values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| BulletProfile | default/bullet/blitz/engine/chaos | weight + safety preset |
| Candidates | 1..24 | MultiPV width |
| Depth | 1..30 | candidate generation depth |
| MaxEvalLossCp | 0..1000 | hard safety gate override |
| LogDb | path | SQLite decision log |

`go wtime btime winc binc / movetime / depth / infinite` all honored.

## BulletLab web platform

`python scripts/web.py --port 8000` → http://127.0.0.1:8000

Lichess-inspired analysis workstation with our own branding and one key
differentiator: **Stockfish evaluation and Bullet (practical) evaluation are
shown as separate concepts everywhere.** Bullet eval is always labeled
`experimental` with the tooltip: *"estimates practical difficulty + winning
potential under time pressure — not objective truth."*

name: clash
readme_excerpt:
# CLASH — Find your next round.

Combat-sports sparring partner matchmaking: fighters create profiles, discover
compatible partners, send sparring requests, browse real Bengaluru gyms and join them.
Strava + Lichess-style matchmaking + social, for combat sports.

## Tech stack

- **Frontend:** Next.js 14 (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS, mobile-first
- **Backend:** Next.js REST API routes (service layer in `lib/`, no business logic in components)
- **Database:** JSON-file prototype store (`data/db.json`) behind `lib/db.ts`.
  Schema mirrors the Postgres design below — swap the backend for Prisma/Postgres
  without touching the UI or API shapes.
- **Auth:** `AuthService` abstraction (`lib/auth.tsx`): `login/logout/getCurrentUser/register`.
  Mock email store now; swap for Supabase Auth / Clerk / Firebase later.
- **Storage:** `POST /api/photos` validates uploads; prototype persists data-URLs on the
  profile, production uploads to Supabase Storage/S3 and stores `photo_url`.

## Architecture

```
Web UI (app/ + components/)
  ↓ fetch + x-user-email header
REST API (app/api/*)          ← thin, validates input
  ↓
Service layer (lib/db.ts, lib/match.ts, lib/seed-fighters.ts)
  ↓
Database (data/db.json now; Postgres later) / Storage
```

Android/iOS can call the exact same REST API. Typed clients live in `lib/api/`
(`fightersApi`, `gymsApi`, `requestsApi`, `usersApi`→`meApi`); shared types in `types/`.

## Database schema (relational design)

`User → FighterProfile → GymMembership → Gym`;
`FighterProfile → FighterSport → CombatSport` (folded into `disciplines[]` in the prototype);
`FighterProfile → SparringRequest → FighterProfile`;
plus `Notification`, `Photo` (`photo_url`), `SavedFighter`, `Availability`
(folded into `availability_days/times`). UUIDs (prefixed), timestamps,
indexes planned on weight/height/age/location/gym_id/skill_level/primary_discipline.

## Pages

`/home` dashboard · `/discover` (filters + bottom-sheet on mobile) · `/fighters` ·
`/fighters/[id]` · `/gyms` · `/gyms/[id]` · `/requests` (received/sent/accepted tabs) ·
`/profile` · `/profile/edit` (6-step onboarding) · `/settings` · `/notifications` ·
`/auth/login` · `/auth/register`

## API

```
GET    /api/fighters?query&w_min&w_max&h_min&h_max&age_min&age_max&skill&fights&discipline&style&intensity&days&times&distance_km&gym_id&gender&sort&limit
GET    /api/fighters/recommended
GET    /api/fighters/search?q=boxing+HSR
GET    /api/fighters/{id}            PATCH /api/fighters/{id}   POST /api/fighters
POST   /api/fighters/{id}/block|report (safety: hide + cancel pending, file report)
GET    /api/gyms?query&discipline&locality&distance_km
GET    /api/gyms/{id}   GET /api/gyms/{id}/members
POST   /api/gyms/{id}/join   DELETE /api/gyms/{id}/leave

name: gaze_scroll
readme_excerpt:
# Gaze Scroll (WebGaze)

Experimental, browser-only eye-tracking scrolling system: look toward the
lower region of a page and the system infers *intentional* downward
movement, then scrolls smoothly. Brief glances never scroll.

**Pipeline:** webcam → gaze estimation → calibration → filtering →
fixation/movement analysis → intent engine → scroll controller → webpage.
See `ARCHITECTURE.md`; heuristics and thresholds in `ALGORITHMS.md`;
comparison protocol in `EXPERIMENTS.md`.

## Run

```bash
cd gaze_scroll
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173
npm test           # 27 unit tests (synthetic gaze sequences)
npm run build
```

Requirements:

- Chrome / Edge / Firefox / Safari with webcam access.
- A **secure context**: `localhost` or HTTPS. Do not open via `file://`
  (`getUserMedia` will refuse).
- Internet on first load: WebGazer (`cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/webgazer@2.0.1`)
  plus MediaPipe face-mesh files (pinned CDN, configured in
  `src/config.js`). Close other tabs holding the camera.

## Use (primary experience)

1. Click **Enable camera & tracking** and allow webcam access.
2. **Calibrate**: read the guidance card, look at each dot and click it
   (5-point fast or 9-point thorough). Skippable for experimentation.
   You get a quality score (good/fair/poor) at the end.
3. **Reading mode**: pick a scroll mode (start with Smooth continuous),
   tick **Enable automatic scrolling**, and read. Sustain confident
   downward gaze to scroll; resume reading to stop; look up to go back.
4. Your wheel, arrow/space keys, or touch **always override instantly**;
   the red **Stop scrolling** button kills automation immediately.

## Developer mode (Gaze Lab)

The on-page Gaze Lab shows live gaze/normalized coords, confidence,
velocity, persistence, fixation, direction, intent + confidence with a
per-signal breakdown, scroll velocity, tracking status, calibration
quality, and gaze target — plus a raw-vs-filtered trajectory canvas, an
event stream (fixations, movements, edge dwells, tracking loss), tunable
parameters, session recording/export (JSON, numbers only), and replay
(play/pause/restart/speed) that re-drives the full pipeline **without a
webcam**. Switch modes during replay to compare strategies on identical
data.

## Privacy

- Webcam access is required; all video processing is **on-device**.
- No video frames are sent anywhere, recorded, or persisted.
- Session exports contain only anonymized gaze-derived numbers and only
  on explicit export clicks. Calibration metadata stays in localStorage.

name: geb
readme_excerpt:
# GEB / Gödel journey

A long-form interactive mathematical documentary that constructs Gödel's First Incompleteness Theorem from formal systems through encoding, diagonalization, truth, and the Halting Problem.

## Run locally

From this folder:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Then open:

```text
http://localhost:8000
```

The entry page is the single coherent journey in `index.html`. It uses Three.js from a browser CDN for the persistent proof-machine scene.

The earlier exploratory probes remain available at `experiments.html` as research artifacts, not as the main experience.

## Notes
The page distinguishes source framing, standard mathematics, toy models, and visual metaphors. It is intentionally explicit about the assumptions behind the incompleteness argument.

name: human-broker
readme_excerpt:
# Lattice / Human Broker

A production-oriented prototype of an AI-first, permission-aware human discovery network. The primary primitive is not a feed: it is **human intent → AI understanding → authorized discovery → consented introduction → conversation → outcome feedback**.

## What is implemented

- Conversational onboarding with provenance-aware fact extraction and editable private model
- Independent profile, discovery, search, category introduction, DM, and contact policies
- Context-specific public/professional/service/dating search projections
- One tool-using Broker for people, introductions, profile, memory, and conversations
- Structured intent and follow-up state; PostgreSQL FTS index + native pgvector recall + deterministic constraints
- Evidence-grounded candidate cards (no public compatibility scores)
- Introduction accept/decline/more-context workflow; acceptance grants DM access
- Permission-checked messaging and inbox summarize/draft/triage endpoints; no auto-send
- Block/report/reputation/product-event persistence foundations
- OpenAI-compatible AI Gateway with structured Broker planning and telemetry
- 120 deterministic fictional users including restrictive Alex Mercer
- Security/unit tests and synthetic evaluation cases
- Responsive AI-native Next.js UI

## Architecture

Next.js calls a FastAPI modular monolith through a same-origin proxy. `BrokerService` asks the configured model for a schema-validated plan, resolves references from server-owned session state, and dispatches a narrow `BrokerTools` method. Services contain workflows; pure domain modules contain policies/scoring; SQLAlchemy persists to PostgreSQL/pgvector. Redis is an optional future job transport. See [stage 2 audit](docs/stage2-audit.md), [architecture](docs/architecture.md), [privacy](docs/privacy.md), [matching](docs/matching.md), [person model](docs/person-model.md), [AI](docs/ai.md), [security](docs/security.md), and [evaluation](docs/evaluation.md).

## Local setup

Requirements: Docker, Python 3.11–3.13, Node 20+.

```bash
cd human-broker
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up -d
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e 'apps/api[dev]'
npm install
npm run seed
```

Run in two terminals (keep PostgreSQL running; if search reports `database_unavailable`, run `docker compose up -d postgres`):

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
cd apps/api && uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

```bash
npm run dev
# open http://localhost:3000
```

The Broker requires a real AI provider. The default configuration uses OpenCode Go at `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` with `glm-5.2` for reasoning, fast operations, and evaluation. Set `AI_PROVIDER=opencode_go` and `AI_API_KEY`; `AI_EMBEDDING_MODEL` may remain empty because the first Broker flow uses local deterministic vectors in PostgreSQL. OpenCode Go protocol routing is model-aware: GLM/Kimi use Chat Completions while GPT-5.6 Luna uses Responses. If the key is absent, Broker requests return an explicit configuration error; deterministic providers are used only by tests.

Verify provider connectivity without exposing the key:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/ai/diagnostics/test \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"Reply with exactly BROKER TEST OK"}'
```

name: infinite_zoom
readme_excerpt:
# Infinite Zoom Camera — V0.1

A working, installable Android camera app and the foundation for AI-powered
"infinite zoom": pinch-zoom with CameraX, still capture, on-device
super-resolution (ONNX Runtime), and an enhanced-result viewer. Fully offline
after install — no cloud, no accounts, no analytics.

> Honesty note: super-resolution *reconstructs plausible detail* from what was
> captured; it cannot literally recover information the sensor never recorded.
> V0.1 demonstrates the real pipeline (capture → crop → SR → display) that
> recursive/generative zoom will build on.

## Architecture

```
app/src/main/java/com/infinitezoom/
  camera/
    MainActivity.kt     orchestration: permission, model init, shutter flow
    CameraController.kt CameraX (Preview + ImageCapture + RGBA analysis stream)
    CameraScreen.kt     full-screen preview + pinch-to-zoom + overlays
    ZoomController.kt   UI gesture <-> camera abstraction (pure Kotlin, tested)
    LivePreviewController.kt  live digital zoom + live AI loop past hw max
  ml/
    SuperResolutionModel.kt  interface + UpscaleResult/timings + exceptions
    OnnxSuperResolution.kt   ONNX Runtime session, ESPCN x3, tiled inference
    ImageTensorUtils.kt      Y-extract / YCbCr-merge, BT.601
    TileMath.kt              native-res tiling math (pure Kotlin, tested)
  pipeline/
    ZoomPipeline.kt          processCapture(image, zoom) -> PipelineResult
    ReconstructionState.kt   ReconstructionState, CropMath, timings
  ui/
    CameraUi.kt         ZoomBadge, ShutterButton, overlays, permission screen
    ResultScreen.kt     enhanced viewer: Original/Enhanced toggle + timings
assets/models/
  super-resolution-10.onnx  bundled ESPCN model (see models/README.md)
```

Conceptual pipeline:

```
logicalZoom -> physical camera zoom -> crop -> SR -> reconstructed image
```

`ZoomController` distinguishes `logicalZoom` (UI) from `physicalZoom`
(CameraX): logical zoom may exceed the physical maximum by up to 8x
(capped at 64x) — the headroom is "reconstruction zoom", cropped tighter
than the preview and restored by SR. The badge turns amber with an "SR" tag
past the hardware limit. Pinch gain grows gently with zoom so traversing
high magnifications doesn't feel like wading (unity at 1x, capped).
`ReconstructionState` carries `reconstructionLevel`.

## Super-resolution pipeline

1. Shutter → `ImageCapture` still frame saved as JPEG → decoded to Bitmap
   (file-based capture; EXIF-oriented upright, OOM-safe downsample retry).
2. The frame is pre-cropped to the screen aspect (WYSIWYG: the preview
   center-crops to the display), then center-cropped by the *extra* digital
   portion only — `logical / physical` — because CameraX zoom already applies
   to the captured frame. Stills carry no in-frame zoom, so extra == logical.
3. The crop is covered with 224×224 tiles at native resolution (aspect

name: jobhunter
readme_excerpt:
# JobHunter — AI job-search & application agent (local-first)

Production-quality local app: discovers real jobs (Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby/RemoteOK/HN public APIs),
analyzes fit vs your structured profile, prepares grounded application material, drives a real
Playwright browser to fill forms, **stops before Submit for explicit human approval**, and tracks
everything in PostgreSQL.

LinkedIn/Wellfound are marked **unavailable** (login-gated + anti-bot) — never circumvented.

## Quickstart

```bash
cp .env.example .env            # add AI_API_KEY (optional; rules engine works without it)
docker compose up --build       # db + backend + frontend
# or local dev:
cd backend && pip install -r requirements.txt && playwright install chromium

readme_title: MusicalBook — an adaptive soundtrack for reading
readme_excerpt:
# MusicalBook — an adaptive soundtrack for reading

An experimental web experience testing one idea: **can a dynamically timed,
pre-generated soundtrack make reading fiction more immersive?**

A reader enters their reading speed (WPM), presses start, and reads Poe's
*The Tell-Tale Heart* while a cinematic score unfolds underneath —
scene changes land where the reader is *expected* to be, computed from
`word_position / WPM × 60`. No accounts, no backend, no live AI: the site
is fully static.

```
Landing → WPM (+ external speed test ↗) → Begin →
reading + adaptive soundtrack → feedback (local only)
```

## Run it

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # develop
npm run build      # static production build → dist/
npm run preview    # serve the production build locally
```

Deploys as-is to Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, or GitHub Pages
(relative `base: './'` — sub-path hosting works).

## Where things live

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `content/story.json` | The story (structured paragraphs; word count is computed, never hand-entered) |
| `content/music-plan.json` | Offline musical analysis: 7 narrative scenes, emotion scores, ACE-Step prompts |
| `content/timeline.json` | Slim runtime timeline **derived** from the plan (`npm run build:timeline`) |
| `public/audio/` | Soundtrack assets, one per scene (probed `.opus → .mp3 → .m4a → .wav`) |
| `src/story/` | WPM → timestamp mapping (`buildTimeline`) |
| `src/audio/` | Playback engine: `AudioEngine.ts`, pure `AudioTimeline.ts`, `crossfade.ts` |
| `src/components/` | `LandingPage`, `ReadingView`, `FeedbackView` |
| `src/config.ts` | All tunables: speed-test URL, WPM bounds, crossfade, preload |
| `tools/music-pipeline/` | Offline creator tooling (LLM prompt, schema, validator) |
| `scripts/` | `generate-placeholders.mjs`, `verify-timing.mjs` |

The browser bundles only `story.json` + `timeline.json`. Analysis scores
and generation prompts never ship to readers.

## How the WPM mechanism works

```
scene_start_time = start_word / WPM × 60
```

Same files, any speed: word 761 (the vulture eye opens) lands at 456s for
100 WPM and 91s for 500 WPM. Each scene bed loops; the next scene starts
fading in `crossfadeSeconds` (default 8s, auto-clamped to scene length)
before its boundary. Pause freezes the clock *and* the audio together, so
resume never loses sync. Progress shown is expected-timeline progress —
this version deliberately does no scroll tracking or live WPM estimation.

Verify it offline: `npm run verify:timing` (boundary math at 100/200/300/500

name: phoneaway
readme_excerpt:
# PhoneAway — Android screen-distance coach

PhoneAway is a small, privacy-first Android utility. While monitoring is enabled, it briefly opens the front camera at a configurable interval, checks whether a face is approximately facing the screen, estimates viewing distance, updates a persistent notification, and gives one short vibration after a sustained too-close episode.

> Camera frames are processed locally and are not stored or transmitted.

This is an ergonomic reminder, not a measuring instrument or medical advice.

## Platform/UX decision

A normal Android app cannot draw into or recolor an arbitrary area of the system status bar. Android also requires notification small icons to be alpha-only and System UI applies its own tint, so a genuinely multicoloured status-bar glyph is prohibited. PhoneAway uses the closest native alternative: an ongoing low-importance foreground-service notification whose title always includes an explicit 🟢/🟡/🔴/⚪ state symbol and whose full-colour large circle icon is regenerated whenever state changes. The compact status-bar glyph remains intentionally monochrome. No overlay permission is requested.

Modern Android also forbids ordinary background camera use. Monitoring runs as a user-started **camera foreground service**, declared with `foregroundServiceType="camera"`, and displays an ongoing notification. On Android 14+, a camera foreground service must be started while the app is visible (the app does this when the switch is enabled); it cannot silently restart from boot or be created later from the background. If Android kills it, monitoring remains stopped until the user opens PhoneAway and starts it again. Android's green camera privacy indicator appears during each sample and cannot/should not be bypassed.

Android 13+ notification permission is requested alongside camera permission. A denied notification permission does not exempt the app from foreground-service rules (the service still appears in system task management), but it makes the status experience poor; grant it for the intended indicator. Camera permission is always required. Persistent notifications may still be exposed to user/OEM controls.

## Architecture

- `monitoring/MonitoringService`: user-started foreground service, screen-on scheduling, lifecycle/error handling.
- `monitoring/CameraSampler`: CameraX 640×480 short bursts; requires three consistent detections, then immediately unbinds/releases camera.
- `vision/`: ML Kit on-device face geometry, coarse looking heuristic, pinhole estimate, median smoothing, hysteretic classifier.
- `notifications/`: ongoing minimal status notification.
- `haptics/`: sustained-episode and cooldown gate.
- `settings/`: Preferences DataStore.
- `state/`: small in-process diagnostic/current-state store.
- Compose UI: onboarding, controls, state, and hidden debug panel (tap the **Screen Distance** title).

No network permission, analytics SDK, account, server, image capture, recognition, or identity tracking is included.

## Distance estimate

The estimator uses the pinhole relationship:

`distance ≈ focalLengthPixels × assumedFaceWidth / detectedFaceWidthPixels`

It converts Camera2 active-array/physical sensor dimensions and focal length into pixel focal lengths after accounting for sensor and CameraX aspect-ratio crops. Width and height estimates are combined when geometrically consistent, with more weight on the steadier width measurement; moderate head pose is projection-compensated. Each check discards two exposure-settling frames, rejects clipped, tiny, oddly proportioned, off-axis faces, and requires three distance measurements agreeing within 12%. A conservative 65° fallback is used when metadata is unavailable. It assumes a 14 cm face width and 19 cm face height, then applies a conservative empirical scale because ML Kit's face box commonly spans less than the assumed physical dimensions. Faces, lenses, detector boxes, and camera metadata differ, so displayed centimeters are approximate. Classification reliability—not physical precision—is the goal.

For device/user calibration, select a preferred distance, physically hold the phone at that measured distance, wait for a stable reading, and press **Calibrate at … cm**. This stores a local multiplicative scale factor; no image or biometric data is retained. Calibration should be performed looking straight at the camera in good light.

"Looking" means a face is found, centered reasonably, and within ±25° yaw/pitch. It is not eye-gaze tracking. `NO_FACE`/`NOT_LOOKING` never warns.

## State stability and haptics

Five recent valid estimates are median-filtered and lightly exponentially smoothed. The selected preferred distance (25 cm by default, adjustable from 25–60 cm) is the warning boundary; recovery requires 4 cm more distance. Sensitivity controls the yellow approach band. A too-close episode must persist for 3 seconds before a 120 ms vibration. It warns only once until recovery, with a configurable persisted cooldown (120 seconds by default).

Because the default sample interval is 15 seconds and each sample releases the camera after one analyzed frame, a 3-second sustained condition is practically confirmed by subsequent periodic samples. This intentionally favors low battery use over immediate warnings.

## Battery strategy

- One short low-resolution burst per selectable 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, or 30 second interval (15 seconds default); two exposure-settling frames are discarded and three consistent detections are required.
- Camera unbound immediately after a stable result (at most eight frames); no preview, recording, bitmap retention, wake lock, or continuous stream.
- No samples while the screen is off (`PowerManager.isInteractive`).
- Fast-mode on-device ML Kit detector.
- Debug-only structured Logcat timings; hidden UI reports samples and average inference time.

## Build

Requirements: Android SDK 34, JDK 17, and Gradle 8.7. This repository includes the Gradle wrapper after bootstrap.

# ProspectPilot — AI-powered B2B prospect research & outreach-prep MVP

Research agent: describe the businesses you want → discover candidates from
public web sources → research their public websites → extract **publicly
displayed** business contacts (with source URLs + confidence/status) →
qualify against your explicit criteria → draft personalized outreach.

**Boundaries (by design):** research + drafts only. No bulk messaging, no
auto-sending. Every draft needs explicit approval, and approval only marks it
`approved_for_sending` — sending is not implemented.

## Architecture

```
campaign brief → CampaignPlanner → DiscoveryAgent (SearchProvider)
  → WebsiteResearchAgent (HTTP + robots.txt + rate limits; Playwright only if needed)
  → ContactExtractionAgent (deterministic regex first, never guesses emails)
  → QualificationAgent (scores ONLY on explicit criteria + stored evidence)
  → OutreachAgent (drafts, every claim traceable to evidence)
```

- `backend/app/agents/` — the six workers above
- `backend/app/providers/` — `SearchProvider` (mock / configurable API),
  `LLMProvider` (mock / OpenAI-compatible via `AI_*`), website fetch+extract
- `backend/app/services/pipeline.py` — async orchestration (idempotent,
  per-item try/except, cancellation, progress counts)
- `backend/app/workers/` — Redis+RQ when `REDIS_URL` is set, else inline
  background threads (same API)
- DB: PostgreSQL via `DATABASE_URL` (SQLite default for local/demo);
  SQLAlchemy models with UUID PKs: campaigns, prospects, contacts,
  research_records, research_evidence, outreach_drafts, suppression_records, agent_runs
- UI: server-rendered dashboard (`/campaigns`, `/campaigns/new`,
  `/campaigns/[id]`, `/prospects/[id]`) + JSON API + `frontend/` static mirror

## Installation

```bash
cd prospectpilot
cp .env.example .env
cd backend
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Environment variables

| Var | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | SQLAlchemy URL (PG in prod, SQLite locally) | `sqlite:///./prospectpilot.db` |
| `REDIS_URL` | empty = inline threads; set = Redis+RQ | empty |
| `SEARCH_PROVIDER` | `mock` \| `configurable_api` | `mock` |
| `SEARCH_API_URL` / `SEARCH_API_KEY` / `SEARCH_API_MODE` | your search API (`serper`/`tavily`/`brave`/`generic`) | empty |
| `AI_PROVIDER` | `mock` \| `openai_compatible` | `mock` |
| `AI_BASE_URL` / `AI_API_KEY` / `AI_MODEL` | any OpenAI-compatible endpoint | `gpt-4o-mini` |
| `RESPECT_ROBOTS_TXT`, `RATE_LIMIT_PER_DOMAIN_SEC`, `FETCH_TIMEOUT` | politeness | true / 1.0 / 15 |
| `DEMO_MODE` | show demo hints in UI | true |

Never commit `.env`. API keys never reach the frontend.

name: rune
readme_title: RUNE — open-web lossless music discovery & streaming for Android
readme_excerpt:
# RUNE — open-web lossless music discovery & streaming for Android

Rune is an open-source online lossless music discovery and streaming client.
The core loop:

**Search the open music web → inspect source/license/audio quality → stream FLAC directly → nothing stored.**

It looks like a riced Linux music app that escaped into Android: near-black OLED
surfaces, monospace instrumentation readouts (`FLAC · 24 BIT · 96 KHZ`), sharp
corners, dense information. It does not look like Spotify.

> **Status: online-first MVP.** Federated search across Internet Archive,
> Jamendo, Openverse, Wikimedia Commons (+ Funkwhale instances, VK explicitly
> UNSUPPORTED), progressive results with filters, per-track stream picker,
> direct Media3 streaming with bounded cache, source fallback, favorites /
> playlists / history as metadata only. Local library code is retained but
> deprioritized as a workflow.

## Product principle

Rune is **not** a piracy application, **not** a local player, **not** a
downloader. Remote sources are used through official/public/authorized
interfaces only:

- source URL, provider, license, attribution and rights metadata are preserved
- unknown rights render as **UNKNOWN LICENSE**, never as "free"
- Creative Commons variants are distinguished, never collapsed to "FREE"
- no DRM/auth/rate-limit/geo circumvention, no scrapers for protected content
- providers without an authorized path (VK) are marked **UNSUPPORTED**

## Features

- Federated search: concurrent per-source queries with timeout, cancellation,
  error isolation, progressive merge, per-source status
- Result grouping (conservative dedup), relevance/quality ranking, inline
  filters (format, license, source, min sample rate) + sorting
- Track screen with AVAILABLE STREAMS picker, provenance, license, source page
- Direct streaming via ExoPlayer (range requests/buffering, no pre-download),
  bounded LRU stream cache (off/128M–1G), CONNECTING/BUFFERING/PLAYING states
- Source fallback: manual "TRY ANOTHER SOURCE" + optional auto-fallback;
  queue items resolve alternates for the same logical track
- Home search hero, sources health, Library = playlists/favorites/history
  (metadata references only — "SOURCE NO LONGER AVAILABLE", never silent loss)
- Media3 service: background, MediaSession, notification, lock-screen,
  headset/Bluetooth, audio focus, noisy-event pause
- Jamendo client id via BuildConfig/gradle property/env or Settings override —
  never in source control

## Architecture

```
SearchScreen → SearchViewModel → FederatedSearchManager → MusicSources (set)
TrackScreen  → RemoteTrackResolver → adapter.getAudioSources (detail only)
PlayerManager → MediaController → RunePlaybackService (ExoPlayer + SimpleCache)
Room: remote_tracks, search_history, playlists, favorites, play_history…
```

- UI never touches source APIs; every source implements `MusicSource`.
- The DB is a metadata index: tracks/albums/artists facts, licenses, artwork
  URLs, favorites, history, playlists, search history. Never audio.

## Vercel Vercel’s AI Cloud is a unified platform for building modern applications, giving teams the tools to be flexible, move fast, and stay secure while focusing on their products instead of infrastructure. ## Deploy Get started by [importing a project](https://vercel.com/new), [choosing a template](https://vercel.com/templates), or using the [Vercel CLI](https://vercel.com/docs/cli). Then, `git push` to deploy. ## Native CLI binaries The standard npm installation remains unchanged: ```bash npm i -g vercel ``` Native CLI binaries are distributed separately and do not affect the `vercel` npm package. To opt into the native binary and replace existing global `vercel` and `vc` commands, install the native package explicitly: ```bash npm i -g @vercel/vc-native --force ``` The `--force` flag allows npm to replace existing global `vercel` and `vc` bin links. Users who do not install `@vercel/vc-native` continue using the regular Node.js-based CLI from `npm i -g vercel`. Platform-specific packages are also available for direct installation when a specific binary is needed: ```bash npm i -g @vercel/vc-native-darwin-x64 --force ``` ## Documentation For details on how to use Vercel, check out our [documentation](https://vercel.com/docs). ## Contributing This project uses [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/) to install dependencies and run scripts. You can use the `vercel` script to run local changes as if you were invoking Vercel CLI. For example, `vercel deploy --cwd=/path/to/project` could be run with local changes with `pnpm vercel deploy --cwd=/path/to/project`. When contributing to this repository, please first discuss the change you wish to make via [Vercel Community](https://community.vercel.com/tags/c/community/4/cli) with the owners of this repository before submitting a Pull Request.
